Press enter or click to view image in full size Illustration generated with Gemini; concept and art direction by the author A product team that starts with “we should add AI” has skipped the most useful step. AI product discovery works best when a team starts from a specific user problem and a measurable product decision, then tests whether AI is the right way to solve it before anyone writes production code. That order protects product managers from building impressive features that nobody needs. The term covers two different jobs. One is using AI to speed up research, such as summarizing feedback or clustering support tickets. The other is discovering whether an AI feature belongs in the product at all. Both differ from ecommerce product discovery, which is about helping shoppers find items. Product teams often blur these together, and the result is a roadmap item with a model attached and no clear user outcome. A simple canvas helps. It asks seven questions in order, from user pain to the evidence that would justify expanding, changing, or stopping a feature. With it, a team can decide what to prototype, what to measure, and when to walk away.
